title: Northbound Systems - Renewal & Growth: Capacity Commitment Alignment + Edge Activation
next_steps: Redwood to send updated pricing & SOW with EU-edge addendum
SE to run 48hr benchmark with customer's sample traffic and share results
Customer to confirm preferred activation window for dedicated nodes (wk of May 24)
Procurement to review updated contract and provide feedback by May 20
action_items: Jonas Reed - run 48hr throughput + p50/p95 latency benchmark using nb-sys sample dataset - due 2027-05-18
Maya Patel - share revised pricing table with committed tokens, burst rules, and EU on-prem addendum - due 2027-05-14
Rita Chen - confirm internal compliance stakeholders and provide SOC2 contact - due 2027-05-17

summary: Renewal check-in focused on aligning capacity commitments and phasing in EU edge. Customer prefers hybrid approach: keep hosted for North America, provision dedicated EU nodes with optional on-prem pilot. Key asks: detailed pricing for committed + burst, audit log retention, KMS integration, run a Redwood SE benchmark on their sample traffic, and set activation window. Next steps agreed: Redwood sends SOW/pricing; SE runs benchmarks; procurement reviews contract.
topics: EU edge/dedicated nodes vs hosted fallback
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Maya from Redwood, jonas and iris with me.
[00:10] Rita Chen: Hi all, Rita here, VP Eng at Northbound. Samir, Lina, Aaron with me.
[00:18] Jonas Reed: Hey, Jonas SE. Quick agenda - align on renewal numbers, discuss EU edge activation, and next steps for a pilot.
[00:30] Samir Kapoor: Yeah thanks. We're still happy with latency on hosted in US but need lower p95 in EU for our customers there. Also wanna understand cost impact if we do committed capacity plus burst.
[00:45] Maya Patel: Totally. Today we can propose a hybrid: keep hosted for NA and spin dedicated EU nodes for regional traffic, with automatic fallback to hosted if spikes exceed capacity.
[00:58] Aaron Mills: Clarify "dedicated" — is that Redwood Dedicated with reserved GPU pools? And can we run a small on-prem pilot in our London DC?
[01:08] Jonas Reed: Yes, Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools, autoscaling policies. On-prem pilot is possible, we call that Private (VPC/on-prem). For the EU pilot we can run a 3-node pilot with your infra for a limited time. Some caveats on network egress and NTP — we'll document.
[01:28] Lina Park: Procurement: need to see SOW and specific pricing tiers. Also, retention for audit logs — our security team requires 12 months.
[01:36] Maya Patel: Understood. We can add extended retention as an add-on. Do you need full raw transcripts or summarized event logs?
[01:45] Lina Park: Event logs + request traces at token-level, and KMS integration for keys. SOC2 evidence as well.
[01:52] Samir Kapoor: On the performance side, we need p50 and p95 numbers at our typical sequence lengths (mean 120 tokens, peak 600).
[02:05] Jonas Reed: Great, we can run a 48-hour benchmark using your sample traffic to capture real distributions. We'll report p50/p95 and tail latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens under the committed config and under burst.
[02:19] Rita Chen: How does prefix caching/KV cache work across region? We worry about cold-starts when routing between EU and US.
[02:27] Jonas Reed: We do prefix/KV cache per serving cluster. On dedicated EU nodes the cache lives local, so EU traffic hits warm caches. If it falls back to hosted in US, you'll see higher latency for cold KV population. But we can tune routing policies to prefer EU for region-based requests; fallback only for overload.
[02:47] Samir Kapoor: Also curious about quantization options — we might accept slightly lower quality for cheaper runs on burst.
[02:54] Maya Patel: Yep, Redwood Optimize can propose quantization profiles per model and per traffic class. We can show projected token-cost savings and expected quality delta with your eval set.
[03:05] Aaron Mills: Network / security question: can we plug into our KMS/HSM for key management and get customer-managed keys for at-rest and in-flight?
[03:14] Jonas Reed: You can — for Private deployments we support bring-your-own-KMS and HSM integrations. For Dedicated we offer KMS integration options (via secure links). We'll need some network config details for the on-prem pilot.
[03:28] Lina Park: Any compliance certifications we should call out?
[03:31] Maya Patel: We maintain SOC2 Type 2, and are working toward ISO expansion. We'll attach the compliance pack.
[03:38] Samir Kapoor: On the SLA: we need p99 latency goals for critical routes and a 24/7 on-call option.
[03:45] Iris Gomez: Our enterprise SLA includes a p99 target for pinned dedicated nodes, and 24/7 incident support is available as an add-on. We'll include that in the SOW.
[03:54] Rita Chen: Pricing — sketch it for me: committed tokens per month plus burst pricing? How granular are the tiers?
[04:02] Maya Patel: Typical structure: committed monthly token band with discounted rate; burst above that pays a higher per-token rate. We also add a small infra fee per dedicated node. We'll provide a table with multiple commitment levels and simulated monthly cost given your usage profile.
[04:18] Lisa Park: (laughs) Lina.
[04:20] Jonas Reed: Sorry, small typo earlier — we'll also include estimated cost delta if you opt for quantized variants.
[04:26] Samir Kapoor: For the on-prem trial, how long to spin up?
[04:29] Jonas Reed: For a 3-node pilot, ~2-3 weeks for coordination and provisioning, plus a security review. If we do an air-gapped package there are extra steps.
[04:38] Rita Chen: Timeline wise, we want to close before end of May to hit June activation. Is that feasible?
[04:43] Maya Patel: If procurement reviews the SOW quickly (Lina), we can run the benchmark the week of May 17 and propose EU dedicated activation for the week of May 24.
[04:53] Lina Park: We'll try to get redlines back by May 20.
[04:56] Aaron Mills: A couple technical nitty-gritty items: will we get per-route throttles, and can we set per-token budgeting per route?
[05:04] Jonas Reed: Yes, routing rules support per-route quotas and throttles. We also support token budgets and priority queues, useful to preserve capacity for critical routes.
[05:14] Samir Kapoor: What about fallback quality differences? If EU fails over to hosted in US, are we sure output won't drift too much?
[05:22] Maya Patel: Drift can occur if you use a different model family for fallback. We recommend model pinning and using a compatible lower-cost quantized variant to reduce drift. We'll include guidance in the rollout notes.
[05:33] Rita Chen: Ok let's talk about the benchmark specifics — we need p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and expected RPS for our expected peak (1500 RPS).
[05:44] Jonas Reed: Noted. We'll simulate 48hrs with normal diurnal patterns and a two-hour peak to capture tail behavior.
[05:52] Iris Gomez: I'll coordinate the report template.
[05:56] Maya Patel: Recap & immediate next steps: Jonas runs the benchmark using the NB sample dataset; I'll send revised SOW/pricing with EU edge and retention add-ons; procurement to return redlines. Anything else?
[06:10] Samir Kapoor: Please include a note on A/B canary rollback policy — we want an automatic fallback if quality regresses.
[06:18] Jonas Reed: We'll include canary window settings, automatic rollback triggers based on eval metrics, and tracing hooks.
[06:24] Rita Chen: Great. Thanks everyone.
[06:26] Maya Patel: Thanks — we'll follow up with docs and scheduling notes.
[06:30] [meeting ends]
